purpose: Machine-readable provenance of the reference (Fortran) OpenRadioss oracle used for differential parity. Every parity claim must cite this file.

upstream.name: OpenCourant/OpenCourant (OpenRadioss)
upstream.git_subject: Add three-surface RHT solid USER01 material and verification tools
upstream.mirror_method: git archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -x  (no .git in the mirror, $OR_SRC never written)

extlib.reason_upstream_url_unreachable: EXTLIB_VERSION.json still points at the pre-move OpenRadioss organisation. From this machine every repository under github.com/OpenRadioss answers 404 (including OpenRadioss/OpenRadioss itself; `gh api orgs/OpenRadioss/repos` returns []), while github.com and unrelated release-asset downloads answer 200/404-with-404-for-all-assets: a known-good asset (psf/numpy v2.4.6) also 404s, so GitHub release-asset downloads are blocked generally, not just for that organisation. No URL, in any organisation, can serve extlib.zip.

incompatible_with_pinned_source.harvested_version: same binaries as extlib v59 (libh3dwriter.so, 759048 bytes, dated 2026-01-21; byte-identical in the extlib mirror and in the 2026-06 / 2026-08 Docker images checked)
incompatible_with_pinned_source.required_by_pinned_source: the h3d API additions that landed in extlib between v59 (2026-05-28) and v82 (2026-09-22)
symptoms: common_source/output/h3d/h3d_build_cpp/h3d_dl.c:260,281,1373,1412 -> error: unknown type name 'H3D_NF_FORMAT'; did you mean 'H3D_DS_FORMAT'?  (the datatype/dataset entry points gained an H3D_NF_FORMAT argument; all 77 call sites pass H3D_NF_REAL)

starter/source/output/checksum/checksum_list.cpp:27 -> fatal error: h3dpublic_import.h: No such file or directory  (a whole new h3d reader/import header: Hyper3DImportOpen / Hyper3DLookupString / Hyper3DImportClose)
incompatible_with_pinned_source.not_substituted: No stand-in was written for either symbol. h3d is an I/O library; inventing its interface would make every later H3D-related parity claim unsound, so the build is left failing instead.
incompatible_with_pinned_source.runtime_consequence_if_forced: libh3dwriter.so at this vintage exports no node-force entry points (`nm -D --defined-only | grep -ci node` -> 0), and libh3dreader.so is absent entirely, so H3D output could not be trusted even if the compile were forced through.

build.system: cmake -S <mirror> -B <build>/<component> per component; -Dbuild=both in a single run is broken upstream (duplicate `extlib` custom target, starter/CMakeLists.txt:189-193 vs engine/CMakeLists.txt:266-270) and -Dbuild=starter together with -Dstarter=starter_linux64_gf silently produces an empty build system (CMakeLists.txt:18 dereferences the `starter` variable), hence -Dbuild=<component> -Dstarter=starter -Dengine=engine and a rename on install.

patched_in_mirror.change: short-circuit: exit 0 when extlib/hm_reader exists and extlib/P0_HARVESTED is present
patched_in_mirror.why: the `extlib` custom target re-downloads on every build and dies at 0%; without this the build cannot run offline
patched_in_mirror.applied_by: tools/oracle/build_oracle.sh (idempotent, gated on the marker, $OR_SRC never touched)
patched_in_mirror.concern: this is a modification of a file inside the writable mirror; it is deliberate, scripted and reversible, and it does not touch solver code

flags.extra_includes_in_probe_only: none in the deliverable path; the feasibility probe in the report injected a scratch header with gcc -include from /tmp, never from the mirror

build.runtime_library_check: build_oracle.sh runs ldd on each installed binary with the oracle environment and fails if any NEEDED library is unresolved; the link-time 'libcrypt.so.1 ... not found' warning from ld is handled with -Wl,-rpath-link so ld resolves the harvested apr-1's dependency chain instead of warning, and libcrypt.so.1 itself comes from the system (/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypt.so.1).

toolchain.cmake_note: the conda cmake 4.4.3 first on PATH is deliberately NOT used: CMake 4 rejects the `cmake_minimum_required (VERSION 3.15)` compatibility declarations in CMakeLists.txt:5 / starter/CMakeLists.txt:5 / engine/CMakeLists.txt:5
toolchain.python3: 3.14.6 (the component CMakeLists hardcode python3 on non-Windows)
toolchain.system_gfortran_reason: none installed; all Fortran comes from conda-forge

third_party_prebuilt_binaries_note: Two Docker Hub images (ale10tech/openradioss-core, dheiny/openradioss-solver) contain prebuilt starter/engine binaries. They were NOT installed or used as the oracle: the deliverable is a from-source build, and shipping someone else's binary as parity evidence would be unsound.
verification_performed: cmake 3.28.3 configures starter and engine cleanly from the mirror (exit 0, targets created)

both components build 100% with gfortran 15.2.0 under the project's own strict flag set (including -Werror=maybe-uninitialized, which upstream adds for GCC 11/15/16) -- no compiler-flag or source-level workaround was needed
both link and both print their version banner: `starter_linux64_gf -v` -> 'OpenRadioss Starter', `engine_linux64_gf -v` -> 'OpenRadios Engine'

tools/oracle/mirror_and_fetch.sh verifies all 14 extlib paths the two arch flag files require, plus the API currency of h3d/hm_reader, on every run, and refuses to proceed when a stale entry point has no declared adapter
the generated build.make carries the POST_BUILD copy into $OR_BUILD/exec, confirming that install() is a no-op and the move to $OR_ROOT/bin has to be explicit

runtime resolution of the installed binaries is verified with ldd under the oracle environment; the harvested apr-1's libcrypt.so.1 dependency is a real runtime need and is satisfied by the system libcrypt (see build.runtime_library_check)
unblock_options: obtain extlib >= the version in $OR_SRC/EXTLIB_VERSION.json (82); every shim in extlib_shims then becomes unnecessary and the gates stop reporting staleness
make github.com/OpenRadioss reachable again (then run mirror_and_fetch.sh with OR_USE_UPSTREAM_EXTLIB=1 to use upstream load_extlib.py unmodified)
allow GitHub release-asset downloads through the proxy and point EXTLIB at a mirror of OpenRadioss_extlib releases
supply extlib as a local directory or archive and teach mirror_and_fetch.sh to copy it in

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), linked into the starter
extlib_shims.implemented_on: libhm_reader_linux64.so v59 primitive GlobalModelSDIGetIncludesList(char**) and GlobalModelSDICountIncludeFiles(int*), resolved by dlsym from their mangled names; reference semantics in reader/source/solver_interface/source/cfg_reading/GlobalModelSdi.cpp:2666-2693
extlib_shims.trust_statement: the include-file list printed in the starter .out is complete and correct for what the v59 reader loaded; nothing else is affected

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), interposes the v59 one-argument export with the pinned two-argument contract
extlib_shims.trust_statement: fixes a real ABI mismatch: left alone, upstream's two-argument call would have written the count through is_dyna and left num_includes at 0, silently dropping the include-file block from the .out

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), linked into the starter
extlib_shims.implemented_on: GlobalEntitySDICountElementsInPart(int*) (v59) plus GlobalEntitySDIGetId(int*,bool*) as a consistency check; reference semantics in reader/source/solver_interface/source/cfg_reading/GlobalModelSdi.cpp:2561-2585 and cpp_count_elements_in_part.cpp:36-49
extlib_shims.trust_statement: 'does the /PART just read hold at least one element' is answered by the reader's own count of the current entity, which is the contract hm_read_part.F relies on for message 178 and for the element-stack path

extlib_shims.kind: NOT implemented - reports the reader's own error
extlib_shims.implemented_on: nothing: the v59 reader has no structured-ALE-mesh creator (nm -D --defined-only | grep -ci sale finds only the unrelated RadiossAleCfdSph_Card classes). The adapter sets message_value(38) = -1, the reader's own 'mesh not created' code
extlib_shims.trust_statement: any deck using /ALE/STRUCTURED_MESH fails loudly with upstream MSGERROR 3153 (s_ale_message.F90:210-215) instead of silently receiving a mesh of zeros; decks without the keyword never call it (hm_s_ale.F90:106-108)

extlib_shims.implemented_on: nothing at run time: the reachable libh3dwriter.so keeps the entry-point names (Hyper3DDatatypeWrite@@H3D_EXPORT_11.0, Hyper3DDatasetBegin@@H3D_EXPORT_11.0), so the extra argument is passed and ignored
extlib_shims.trust_statement: h3d output is inadmissible anyway (see inadmissible_parity_evidence_reasons.h3d); the node-force dataset feature does not exist in this h3d build

extlib_shims.implemented_on: nothing: the prototypes are transcribed from h3dreader_dl.c and declared weak, so the dynamic linker resolves them from the dlopen'ed libh3dreader.so; if that library is missing the caller has already returned (checksum_list.cpp:645-652)
extlib_shims.trust_statement: /CHECKSUM_REPORT over H3D files is not available (no libh3dreader.so on this box); the checksum report over A-files/T01 is unaffected

extlib_shims.kind: header shim replacing four prototypes via #include_next
extlib_shims.implemented_on: nothing: declarations only, shaped exactly as the pinned call sites pass the arguments (an int such as pool_count cannot be passed implicitly to an enum parameter, so the alternative shape does not even compile)
extlib_shims.trust_statement: h3d element/dataset blocks are written against a library whose ABI is one parameter short, so the arguments after type_id/nf_format shift inside the old callee; h3d output is inadmissible

extlib_shims.implemented_on: nothing: 0 is the honest value, this h3d build can neither disable zlib nor skip the sort (extlib/h3d/includes/h3dpublic_defs.h:171-176 shows the reachable H3D_FileMode layout); inventing bit patterns would set unrelated mode bits
extlib_shims.trust_statement: H3D files keep this library's default compression and sorting; not admissible for parity

extlib_shims.kind: source adapter (C), linked into starter and engine
extlib_shims.implemented_on: Hyper3DExportLibraryVersion reports the loaded library's real export version (readelf -V -> H3D_EXPORT_11.0, i.e. 11.0), which is below the 2612.0 the engine demands, so upstream's own gate fires MSGID 324 + ARRET(2). Hyper3DCompressionLevel only announces on stderr that the level cannot be applied; it is unreachable behind that gate
extlib_shims.trust_statement: a run that requests h3d output is aborted by the solver itself instead of this oracle pretending the library is new enough

inadmissible_parity_evidence_reasons./ALE/STRUCTURED_MESH (S-ALE): the v59 reader has no structured-ALE-mesh creator; the adapter returns the reader's own error -1, so any deck using the keyword fails with MSGERROR 3153 (starter/source/ale/s_ale_message.F90:210-215) instead of producing a mesh
inadmissible_parity_evidence_reasons.H3D animation files: three independent reasons: (1) the reachable libh3dwriter.so is H3D_EXPORT_11.0 while the engine requires >= 2612.0 (engine/source/output/h3d/h3d_results/genh3d.F:734-746), so upstream's own gate aborts the run; (2) Hyper3DElementBegin/Element2Begin gained an H3D_ID type_id, so the old callee sees parent_id/parent_poolname_id/node_poolname_id shifted by one register; (3) the pinned tree disagrees with itself about where H3D_NF_FORMAT sits (call sites 6th/7th, shim wrappers h3d_dl.c:1371-1416 last), so no header choice can repair it. Node-force datasets cannot be written at all (nm -D | grep -ci node -> 0)
inadmissible_parity_evidence_reasons./CHECKSUM_REPORT over H3D files: needs libh3dreader.so, which no reachable extlib contains; the prototypes are weak so the starter runs, but the checksum list cannot be built

parity_evidence_caveats: native .k deck reading goes through hm_reader v59 (plus the three cpp_* adapters above); every keyword read is the library's own, but a future audit should re-check /PART message 178 and the element-stack choice against a build with a current hm_reader
the include-file list in the starter .out comes from the v59 reader's include set; the adapter forwards both the count and the names faithfully
nothing in this oracle was built from a third-party prebuilt binary; the two Docker Hub images that contain prebuilt starter/engine binaries were never installed
